about: Buy good companies, don't overpay, do nothing. US holdings of the UK fund manager.
summary: 41 holdings; the top ten are 52% of the portfolio.
Trades a lot: about 60% of the portfolio changes in a year.
The average holding, by value, has been owned for at least 5.6 years.
Compared with the typical S&P 500 company, its holdings are more expensive, more profitable, faster-growing and much larger.
Copying each filing beat the S&P 500 in 4 of 9 full years.

profile.background: Born in 1953. A top-rated bank analyst in the 1980s, author of Accounting for Growth (1992), then chief executive of Collins Stewart and Tullett Prebon before founding Fundsmith in London in 2010.
profile.approach: In Fundsmith's own words: buy good companies, don't overpay, then do nothing. That means high returns on capital, little debt, and very low trading.
known: Accounting for Growth exposed accounting tricks and became a bestseller.
profile.note: The 13F shows only the US-listed part of Fundsmith's portfolio; its European and other holdings are not included.

name: Terry Smith
